vocabulary.meaning: the system of linked pages and resources accessed through the internet
examples: The World Wide Web changed how people find information.
Millions of websites are available on the World Wide Web.
Open the page in your web browser.
Modern web browsers include privacy and security tools.

vocabulary.meaning: a clickable connection from one webpage or document to another
examples: The article contains a hyperlink to the original study.
Click the hyperlink to open the next page.

vocabulary.meaning: a collection of related pages on the internet
examples: The organisation launched a new website.
Most businesses now maintain a website.

vocabulary.meaning: the global network connecting computers and devices
examples: The web is one service that operates on the internet.
Internet access has become essential for many jobs.

vocabulary.meaning: a single page of information available on the web
examples: The information appears on the university's webpage.
The webpage loads quickly on mobile phones.

vocabulary.meaning: the readable address used to identify a website
examples: The company registered a new domain name.
A short domain name is easier to remember.

vocabulary.meaning: connected to or available through the internet
examples: More public services are now available online.
She completed the course entirely online.

vocabulary.meaning: a new idea, method, or technology
examples: The web was a major technological innovation.
Innovation can change how people communicate.

vocabulary.meaning: a technical rule or format that anyone can use
examples: Open standards helped the web grow rapidly.
Developers can build compatible tools using an open standard.
